2.67 Any improvement to the overall energy situation bears directly on the economic, environmental, and political well-being of the public. Thermal power plants constitute the largest single type industry that consumes fossil fuels in southwestern Texas. They offer the best opprotunity to conserve fuel oil and natural gas.
The Consuming Area
2.68 There are three firms with capabilities for distributing the energy from Amistad to individual consumers on the US side.
(a) The Central Power and Light Company (CP&L) owns and operates a system serving about 44,000 square miles of southern Texas. It is the major power company of the area. Some of the larger cities it serves are Corpus Christi, Laredo, Harlingen, Del Rio, Victoria, Kingsville, and Edinburg (Harza, 1963). It operates generating plants totaling 3,027.7 megawatt (MW) installed capacity. Wide seasonal variations of its system peak demand are typical. Summer peaks in August are about one and one-half the February peaks. Of the total capacity, 2,931.9 MW are gas and (or) oil fired steam turbines, 54.7 MW are gas turbines, and 41.1 MW are hydropower. The hydropower capacity consists of 9.6 MW from the Maverick plant and 31.5 MW purchased from the Falcon plant. A gas-oil steam unit of 351.0 MW is scheduled for service in August 1976. The company is constructing one 550 MW coal-fired steam turbine unit at Fannin, Texas, scheduled for service in 1979. Another 550 MW coal-fired unit is scheduled for completion in 1986. No information is available as to units planned for retirement.
(b) The Medina Electric Cooperative, Inc. operates a distribution system covering 17 counties of southwestern Texas. It serves another co-op covering an additional 4 counties, several small communities and rural customers. It produces 75.0 MW from a plant located at Pearsal, Texas, which consists of one 25.0 MW gas-oil steam turbine unit and two gas turbines of 25.0 MW each.
(c) The South Texas Electric Cooperative, Inc. serves 27 counties in south Texas. To explain the rather complex marketing arrangement of this cooperative and others, the following is extracted from it's report to the Federal Power Commission (FPC Form 12) for 1975.
The South Terms Electric Cooperative, Inc. is a member of two power pools. The first is with the Medina Electric Cooperative, Inc., Hondo, Texas, which pools the electric generating capabilities of each party's generating plants and certain other facilities involved in the second power pool which has as members the two above cooperatives and the Central Power and Light Company.
The South Texas Electric Cooperative is connected to the Medina Electric Cooperative by two 69 kV lines at the Frio-Atascosa County Line. It is normally connected to the Central Power and Light Company by a 138 kV line at Victoria and a 69 kV switching station at Calallen. The Medina Electric Cooperative transmission and generating system is connected to the Central Power and Light Company by a 138 kV line at Moore, Texas.
The two cooperatives operate their combined transmission and generation systems as one. The power plants are operated in such a manner as to produce electric power and energy at the lowest combined cost. Any additional required capacity is purchased from the Central Power and Light Company.
